How It Was Used: Usually paired with classical classifiers after preprocessing or segmentation [4, 2]
Reported Result: In one comparative paper, the best texture-based setup with combined features and Random Forest reached 96.05% accuracy on segmented MRI images; another glioblastoma study reported 100% accuracy with combined GLCM, LBP, and IBA features [4, 5]
Takeaway: GLCM-based features can work well, especially when combined with other texture or intensity descriptors, but the best results usually come from carefully engineered pipelines rather than GLCM alone [4, 5]

How It Was Used: As a handcrafted texture descriptor, often fused with HOG, GLCM, or fed into SVM / CNN / other classifiers [6, 5]
Reported Result: Reported accuracies ranged from about 84.95% for LBP+SVM to 95.6% for CLBP+CNN and 97% for SVM with combined LBP + HOG in one review paper [5, 6, 7]
Takeaway: LBP features are common and competitive, but by themselves they usually lag behind strong deep learning baselines; hybrid CLBP+CNN pipelines narrow the gap [5, 8]

How It Was Used: Often fused with LBP/CLBP or used as input to SVM, RF, or other classifiers [6, 9]
Reported Result: One direct comparison reported RF with Gabor/HOG at 89.40% versus a custom CNN at 96.03%; another CLBP+CNN paper reported 95.6% accuracy [8, 6]
Takeaway: HOG is useful as a handcrafted baseline, but in the papers I found it was usually strongest when fused with other descriptors; pure DL still tends to win on accuracy [8, 6]

How It Was Used: To capture multiresolution texture, often combined with GLCM, LBP, and statistical or geometric features [9, 11, 3]
Reported Result: Reported accuracies include 96.05% for a DT classifier on 31 traditional features, 96% for DWT-LBP plus geometric features with Naive Bayes, and 98.60% F1/accuracy in a DWT-radiomics fusion framework for glioma grading [4, 11, 12]
Takeaway: DWT features are especially common in hybrid feature-engineering pipelines; they can be strong, but they tend to shine when paired with other descriptors rather than standing alone [4, 12]

How It Was Used: Feature extractors such as CLBP, HOG, GLCM, or DWT are combined with CNNs, transfer learning, or CNN-extracted features fed into classical classifiers [2, 5, 1]
Reported Result: These hybrids often land in the 95% to 99% range; examples in this set include 95.6%, 96.0%, 97%, 98.60%, and 99.2% depending on dataset and task [6, 12, 7, 1]
Takeaway: The strongest pattern in the papers I found is not texture features versus deep learning as a pure binary; it is that handcrafted features still matter when they are fused with deep representations, especially for robustness and interpretability [2, 1]
